label: copy-phase input m echoing one of the first two original tokens
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase when the fed-back input token is m, essentially only early in the copy (recall_idx 1-3, i.e. the input is the echo of original token 0, 1 or 2). Magnitude is strongly position-dependent: the largest activations (~0.75-1.0 of max) occur at the first copy step after <DEL> when the sequence started with m (first_tok = m carries ~78% of mass); echoes of original token 1 give ~0.25-0.35 of max, and echoes of original token 2 give weak activations (~0.02-0.1), which are the main misses. Never fires in the original phase or on <DEL>, never on other input tokens, and not on m when it appears later in the copy (recall_idx >= 4). Some short-sequence (L=3-4) m echoes at recall_idx 2 do not fire (false positives).

issues: The factual claims hold up. Every activation is in the copy phase (original and delimiter phases have 0 actives). m carries 100% of the activation mass (only about 60 stray actives on other tokens). first_tok = m carries 0.778 of the mass. recall_idx 1 / 2 / 3 hold 77% / 22% / 1.2% of the mass, and recall_idx >= 4 holds 0.02% (precision 0.003 on m there).
Test scores reproduce exactly: P 0.974, R 0.862, F1 0.915, mass recall 0.988. recall_idx == 1 alone has precision 1.0 and holds 77% of the mass.

Most misses are m at recall_idx 3 (echo of original token 2), firing very weakly (about 0.02-0.08 of max). Only 31% of those steps fire, so adding them hurts the score (F1 0.860 with recall_idx <= 3). Leaving them out is the right call, as the explanation says.

The false positives follow one small systematic rule: m at recall_idx 2 with L == 3 almost never fires (precision 0.014, 442 predicted steps, about half of the 865 false positives). This is m echoed as the second original token in a 3-token sequence. L == 4 is also weaker (precision 0.82). Excluding L == 3 raises test F1 only slightly, from 0.915 to 0.920 (P 0.987). This matches the explanation's note that false positives cluster at L = 3-4, so it is a refinement, not a refutation.
The label and the predicate agree: echoes of original tokens 0 and 1 are recall_idx 1 and 2.
